messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'private-controlplane-vpc' — incident P1. Affected customer: AcmeCorp (private VPC). Symptom: control-plane hostname not resolving from customer subnets. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INC123456

pagerduty: Incident INC123456 created — page routed to on-call. Escalation policy: private-vpc->eng-oncall->sre-leads.

mike: acked. jumping in. I can see repeated DNS timeout from our control-plane resolvers for the customer's VPC.

alex: I'm on network. can we confirm this is DNS and not egress/NAT? quick curl would time out to CP endpoint?

mike: ran a quick curl from our proxy into the customer VPC via the dedicated peering, example:
```bash
curl -v https://controlplane.internal.redwood.acmecorp:443 --max-time 5
# result: * Resolving controlplane.internal.redwood.acmecorp (controlplane.internal.redwood.acmecorp)... failed: Name or service not known.
# curl: (6) Could not resolve host: controlplane.internal.redwood.acmecorp
```

sara: tagging network team. @alex can you traceroute and check route tables, security groups, and VPC DNS settings? I'll look at the on-prem agent side (agent heartbeats).

alex: running traceroute from peering host now.
```bash
traceroute -n 10.12.23.1
# 1 10.12.0.1 0.4 ms
# 2 10.12.99.1 1.2 ms
# 3 10.13.255.254 5.3 ms
# 4 * * *
```

alex: traceroute dies inside customer transit. looks like traffic dropping after their transit gateway. I'm opening contact with Acme NOC (ticket: ACME-9876).

jordan: I can try querying their VPC DNS from a different path (edge egress) to confirm if it's path-specific.

emily: FYI control-plane health shows all components healthy in prod, so likely network path issue only.

mike: checking our agent heartbeats for Acme's on-prem agent (agent-id: ag-0423):
```text
2026-03-14T02:11:34Z agent ag-0423 heartbeat failed: dial tcp: lookup controlplane.internal... no such host
2026-03-14T02:12:34Z agent ag-0423 heartbeat failed: dial tcp: lookup controlplane.internal... no such host
```

sara: restarting agent on their onprem host (remote-run via ssh). will post commands and output.

sara: ssh to proxy host and restart redwood-agent:
```bash
ssh ec2-user@acme-proxy-01
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 50 --no-pager
```

sara: after restart logs show repeated failures to resolve control-plane host. agent restart didn't fix DNS.

mike: okay that points to DNS at customer side (forwarding or route). Contact with Acme NOC: they confirm they rolled a change to their transit gateway earlier and saw BGP flap at ~01:50 UTC. They're reverting a route tweak now (ACME-9876).

jordan: while they revert, can we add a temporary fallback in our routing to reach control-plane via secondary peering? (we have a backup egress path).

emily: we can route requests for Acme to the secondary control-plane endpoint in another region; need approval for cross-region failover for production customer. this will change latency/cost.

mike: proposal: while ACME NOC reverts, set routing policy to fallback->controlplane-alt.acmecorp.internal via our backup peering. manual change on edges will take ~3-5 mins.

sara: i applied the route on edge router cluster (edge-router-3). command:
```bash
# on edge-router-3
ip route add 10.120.0.0/16 via 172.31.9.1 dev eth1 metric 100
```

sara: testing DNS resolution from our agent now:
```bash
dig +short controlplane.internal.redwood.acmecorp @172.31.9.2
# 10.120.5.23
```

mike: confirmed controlplane resolves from backup path. sending a quick smoke from agent:
```bash
curl -sS https://controlplane.internal.redwood.acmecorp:443/healthz | jq .
# {"status":"ok","ts":"2026-03-14T02:22:11Z"}
```

incident-bot: Incident INC123456 status update: customer impact reduced. Fallback route active. Continued monitoring.

pagerduty: Note: INC123456 acknowledged by mike at 1945678910 and escalated to eng-oncall at 1945678999.

alex: leaving a checklist for post-incident: 1) confirm ACME NOC revert succeeded and route stable; 2) schedule RCA with customer & networking; 3) consider automated failover for vpc-dns next time.

sara: pinging Acme to confirm they completed revert. they say revert finished at 02:25 UTC and BGP converged. we're seeing stable traceroutes now.

jordan: I'm taking the handoff for next 2 hours (night oncall). current state: fallback route active, controlplane resolving via backup, agent ag-0423 heartbeats restored. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate if anything regresses.

emily: nice work team. please create a short incident note and tag for follow-up in #postmortems.

mike: summary for handoff -> affected: AcmeCorp private VPC DNS to control-plane. impact: agent heartbeats failed, customer API requests to control-plane failed intermittently. mitigations: applied edge fallback route to alternate peering; coordinated with Acme NOC to revert transit gateway change. status: resolved -> reduced to monitoring.

jordan: acknowledged handoff. will add timeline to incident doc and create the follow-up ticket.

incident-bot: Incident INC123456 marked as "monitoring" by jordan at 1945679275. If any new alerts fire, incident will re-open. :white_check_mark:
